title: Proper geometric-point derived pushforward preserves coproducts
statement: Let Λ be a finite commutative ring, k an algebraically closed field, and p : X → Spec k a proper morphism. The right derived direct-image functor Rp_* on the ordinary unbounded derived categories of small-etale Λ-module sheaves preserves colimits of Discrete I for every I : Type (u+1), where schemes and k lie in Type u and coefficient modules in Type (u+1). No boundedness assumption on the input complexes is made. The derived categories and canonical functors are as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].

source.place: Lemma 59.96.3 and its proof, extended to a finite commutative coefficient ring as in 0F12

proof.text: A proper k-scheme is quasi-compact, separated, and of finite type, hence has finite dimension. The finite coefficient ring is annihilated by a positive integer. The torsion cohomological-dimension bound over a separably closed field, together with the module-cohomology forgetful comparison, gives a uniform finite cohomological bound for module sheaves. Constancy of module sheaves on Spec k identifies these global-cohomology bounds with bounds on the higher direct images. Module-valued cohomology on the qcqs scheme commutes with filtered colimits; express sums as filtered colimits of finite sums to obtain commutation with sums.

Resolve every input complex by a K-injective complex with injective terms. The termwise direct sum represents the derived coproduct. Every term of this sum is direct-image-acyclic because positive higher direct images commute with sums and vanish on each injective summand.

The finite cohomological bound permits computing the unbounded derived functor on the sum complex by taking direct image termwise, although the sum need not be K-injective. Termwise direct image commutes with the sums by the degree-zero comparison. Localizing the resulting natural complex isomorphism identifies the canonical coproduct comparison and proves it invertible. The empty family, empty X, zero ring and zero complexes require no extra cases.
